module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 520

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/520](https://www.erdosproblems.com/520)
- [Hø26] Høystad, S. W. R., *A self-contained Lean 4 proof that Erdős Problem #520 has a
  negative answer* (2026), https://github.com/saasom/Erdos520/blob/v1.1.0/paper/erdos520_note.pdf
- [Ha13] Harper, A. J., *Bounds on the suprema of Gaussian processes, and omega results for the
  sum of a random multiplicative function*. Ann. Appl. Probab. 23 (2013), 584–616.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Nat Real Filter

namespace Erdos520

variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]

/--
A random function $f$ is Rademacher multiplicative if $f(1) = 1$,
for each prime $p$, we independently choose $f(p) \in \{-1, 1\}$ uniformly at random (so each
$f(p)$ is a measurable function of the sample point),
for each square-free integer $n = p_1 \cdots p_r$, $f(n) = f(p_1) \cdots f(p_r)$, and
for each non-squarefree integer $n$, $f(n) = 0$.
-/
structure IsRademacherMultiplicative (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) : Prop where
  /-- Prime entries are random variables. -/
  measurable_of_prime p : p.Prime → Measurable (f p)
  /-- Prime entries are independent. -/
  iIndepFun_primes : iIndepFun (fun p : Primes ↦ f p) ℙ
  /-- Primes entries are uniformly distributed on `{-1, 1}`. -/
  prob_of_prime p : p.Prime → ℙ {ω | f p ω = 1} = 1 / 2 ∧ ℙ {ω | f p ω = -1} = 1 / 2
  map_one ω : f 1 ω = 1
  map_mul_of_coprime a b ω : a.Coprime b → f (a * b) ω = f a ω * f b ω
  map_of_not_squarefree n ω : ¬ Squarefree n → f n ω = 0

/--
Let $f$ be a Rademacher multiplicative function.
Does there exist some constant $c > 0$ such that, almost surely,
$$
  \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{m \leq N} f(m)}{\sqrt{N \log \log N}} = c?
$$

The answer is no: Høystad [Hø26] (with GPT-5.6 Pro and Claude) proved, following the
Halász–Lau–Tenenbaum–Wu–Caich martingale approach with Harper's low-moment estimates [Ha13],
that almost surely $\sum_{m \le N} f(m) \ll \sqrt{N} (\log \log N)^{1/4 + \eta}$ for every
$\eta > 0$, so the $\limsup$ is $0$ almost surely. The linked formal
proof works with the concrete model `ℕ → Bool` with the product of fair coins, whose
squarefree-supported Rademacher function is `IsRademacherMultiplicative`; this refutes the
statement below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 60, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos520.lean#L24"]
theorem erdos_520 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ (Ω : Type) [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
      (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), IsRademacherMultiplicative f →
      ∀ᵐ ω, limsup (fun N ↦ ∑ m ≤ N, f m ω / sqrt (N * log (log N))) atTop = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos520

findings.description: The theorem docstring (line 65) cites [Ha13] for the Harper low-moment estimates used by Høystad. However, [Ha13] is the 2013 Gaussian-suprema and omega-results paper, not the low-moment paper cited for this input in [Hø26]. This is a reference error; the Lean statement is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Høystad, §2.2, identifies the analytic core as Harper's “better than square-root cancellation” phenomenon and cites HarperFMPi. Its bibliography identifies that reference as “Moments of random multiplicative functions, I: Low moments, better than square-root cancellation, and critical multiplicative chaos,” Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020), e1. See https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saasom/Erdos520/v1.1.0/paper/erdos520_note.tex. The cited 2013 paper instead gives Gaussian-supremum estimates and the lower-bound result in Corollary 3 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.0210).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 2020 Harper paper as [Ha20] and replace [Ha13] with [Ha20] in the theorem docstring's attribution of the low-moment estimates.

reformulations.difference: Lean takes the limsup in ℝ, without explicit boundedness assumptions, rather than using an extended-real limsup.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is safe because the requested value c is strictly positive. The real limsup's exceptional cases—an empty set of eventual upper bounds or one unbounded below—both return 0 and therefore cannot equal c. I proved in /workspace/review/limsup_equivalence.lean that for every u : ℕ → ℝ and c > 0, limsup u atTop = c iff limsup (fun n => (u n : EReal)) atTop = (c : EReal). The proof uses only standard axioms.

reformulations.difference: The source fixes a Rademacher random multiplicative function; Lean places the existential constant before universal quantification over all probability spaces and all functions satisfying the predicate.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All such models have the same law: their countable family of prime values has the product law of independent fair signs, and every remaining coefficient is determined by the prime-product formula and squarefree support. The normalized-limsup equality is a measurable event determined by this countable process, so its probability for each fixed c is identical in every model. Thus a constant works for the source's model iff it works uniformly for every Lean model. A concrete fair-coin model satisfying the predicate was constructed in /workspace/review/model_checks.lean; the full distributional equivalence was not formalized.

sources_consulted: Høystad, A self-contained Lean 4 proof that Erdős Problem #520 has a negative answer, v1.1.0: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saasom/Erdos520/v1.1.0/paper/erdos520_note.tex — problem statement, main theorem and corollary, low-moment input, formal-model discussion, and bibliography.

Harper, Bounds on the suprema of Gaussian processes, and omega results for the sum of a random multiplicative function: https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.0210 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1012.0210 — introduction, Rademacher definition, and Corollary 3.

Durkan and Pearce-Crump, A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of random multiplicative functions: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29429 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2607.29429 — introduction, main theorem, corollary, and Harper bibliography entry.

Mathlib at the supplied checkout: Order/LiminfLimsup.lean, Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean, Probability/Independence/Basic.lean and its kernel definitions, Data/Nat/Squarefree.lean, and the real logarithm and square-root definitions.
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. Lean checks established the prime-product formula, measurability of all coefficients, simultaneous almost-sure ±1 prime values, existence of the fair-coin model, and equality with the linked proof's one-indexed normalized sums. Boundary checks covered squarefreeness through 15, f(0)=0, f(1)=1, f(4)=0, f(6)=f(2)f(3), initial zero denominators, and eventual positivity of the normalizer. The linked proof's endpoint and model were inspected, but its entire project was not rebuilt. erdosproblems.com/520 and its status pages remained blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so their live remarks/status could not be checked. Høystad's cited note and the independent Durkan–Pearce-Crump theorem support the recorded solved/negative status.
